thread:
Morgan: FYI onboarding 'orca-lite-8b' from a community repo. Found weights + a LICENSE that looks like `CC-BY-NC-4.0` + a short PATENTS.md. Posting details and a quick question: can we offer quantized derivatives to Dedicated/private customers? :thinking:

Morgan: link: https://github.com/thirdparty/orca-lite (weights in `release/v1`)

Jas: quick read — NC = non-commercial, so selling inference might be a problem. But if we only host for research orgs? Not sure about Dedicated paid customers.

Leah-legal: =leah-legal= Noted. CC-BY-NC restricts commercial use; that can block serving to paying customers and redistribution of derivatives for commercial purposes. Need to check whether "providing inference as a service" counts as commercial under that license (likely yes). Also PATENTS file could add restrictions.

Priya: infra perspective: we planned to ship an 8-bit quantized package (weights+loader) for Private on-prem installs. If license disallows redistribution, we can't include the quantized weights in our installer. We could instead provide model fetch hooks that point to upstream, but that impacts UX.

Sam: from eval side: we're seeing small quality regressions after 8-bit quantization on our dialogue suite. If we can't distribute quantized weights, we could host the quantized runtime internally in Hosted/Dedicated and provide an API. But that still sounds like commercial hosting.

Leah-legal: Agree. Two paths: 1) request a commercial license/exception from upstream (preferred), or 2) limit availability to non-commercial/research customers only and add clear attribution + licensing notice. For Private installs, we can provide only tooling to convert weights client-side (no redistribution).

Morgan: PATENTS.md mentions a "patent grant" but also an "opt-out" clause for certain contributors. I'll paste the excerpt below:

Morgan: ```
Contributor patent grant: grants use for research and internal evaluation.
Exceptions: contributors may withhold patent rights for "commercial distribution" unless separate agreement.
```

Jas: that sounds risky. If contributors can withhold patent rights for commercial distribution, our Hosted/Dedicated offering might infringe. Leah — should we escalate to IP counsel?

Leah-legal: Yes escalate. Please open an intake with IP and include the upstream contact + full license, PATENTS.md, and provenance (where weights came from). Also we need to confirm whether derivatives created by quantization count as "adaptations" under CC terms — likely yes.

Priya: operational ask: can infra-bot run an artifact provenance check and add an SBOM? @infra-bot can you annotate the repo?

infra-bot: Automated scan complete — repo references huggingface mirror and a google drive backup. No signed provenance or contributor CLAs found. Checks: checksum mismatch for one release file (needs human review). :eyes:

Sam: I'll queue the model into our eval pipeline (bench-suite v1.2 + redwood-regressions promptset). Will attach tokenized failure cases and latency numbers. If legal says "no redistribution" we still can benchmark locally and recommend config changes.

Morgan: Action items from this thread: 1) Morgan -> upload LICENSE + PATENTS.md to legal intake ticket, 2) Leah -> open IP intake + advise on commercial hosting risk, 3) Jas -> estimate impact on Dedicated/Private UX if we cannot ship prebuilt weights, 4) Sam -> run evals and post regressions, 5) Priya -> add SBOM/provenance notes to onboarding doc.

Leah-legal: Also add an attribution template (short HTML snippet) we can show in Console if we get permission. CC-BY requires attribution; even for research uses we must show name and source link.

Morgan: will do. tagging @Leah-legal @Jas @Sam @Priya. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
